title: feat(virtual): validate JavaScript and Rust command ecosystems
body:
Fixes #30.

Virtual command packages have executable coverage in JavaScript and Rust for install/create/extend, composition and inheritance, generators and streaming, middleware/plugins, typed interfaces, registry discovery, atomic reload and ownership-aware uninstall. Both languages include ten typed example packages and runnable ecosystem/enterprise demonstrations. The latest main is included, preserving its lightweight core, shared registry, configured builders and subsequent fixes. Invalid-name regressions cover full/core ESM/CommonJS without mutating registry state.

The failing Deno check was caused by esm.sh's GitHub builder returning HTTP 500 with `mkdir /esm/npm/.install-274404154: no space left on device`. The checkout HTTP test and its ShellJS/glob assertions passed before that external compilation failed. [Archived evidence and reproduction](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-30-a0052265/dev/log/issues/30/pulls/116/cdn-fix/README.md) include the original job, a failing regression test, and actual PR/push-policy runs.

The job still requires checkout execution over HTTP with real esm.sh dependencies and still attempts the immutable source import. Only pull requests may skip the hosted compilation probe, with a warning, after a separate request confirms HTTP 500 and the exact disk-full response for the same entry URL. Other HTTP, dependency, compilation and execution failures remain fatal. Main pushes and manual dispatches fail even for this verified outage, with explicit recovery instructions.

**Manual action to restore the strict main check:** ask the esm.sh operator to free storage under `/esm/npm`, then rerun the Deno CDN job. No new secret is required for the mandatory checkout test.

Validation:

- New regression: four failures before the fix; all 16 cases pass after it. Focused CDN/ShellJS suites: 29 passed.
- Full JavaScript suite: **2,939 passed**, 10 skipped, 0 failed; 67,056 assertions.
- Full Rust all-features suite: **984 passed**, seven ignored, 0 failed across 64 suites, including doctests.
- All **37 executable features** agree in Node, Bun and Rust.
- ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript, duplication, Cargo formatting, generated documentation and 473 workflow/layout/documentation tests pass.
- Windows timeout regression: split Git/HTTP integration and retain five-second operation limits; two injected three-second Git starts fail before the fix and pass afterward. Linux CI runs this bounded real-Git reproduction. See the [latency evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-30-a0052265/dev/log/issues/30/pulls/116/cdn-fix/windows-latency.md).
- Actual Deno integration: the PR policy exits zero after all mandatory assertions; the push policy exits one with the required recovery instruction.

The [JavaScript guide](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-30-a0052265/js/docs/VIRTUAL-COMMAND-ECOSYSTEM.md), [Rust guide](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-30-a0052265/rust/docs/VIRTUAL-COMMAND-ECOSYSTEM.md) and [requirement/competitor matrix](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-30-a0052265/docs/VIRTUAL-COMMAND-COMPARISON.md) map capabilities to tests and document constraints. Competing custom-command, plugin and streaming APIs are credited; the supported advantage is the integrated lifecycle across both languages. No parity exemption is present. JavaScript patch and Rust minor release fragments are included.

**Unfinished external success outcomes:** ten independent registry publications, external developer adoption and enterprise production use remain unverified. The October 24 npm query found zero discoverable keyword-tagged packages; `npm whoami` returned `ENEEDAUTH`, with no publishing identity or demonstrated namespace ownership available. Tested examples do not establish those outcomes. Universal superiority over every competitor workload is also unverified. These criteria remain unfinished; this PR remains unmerged. See the [acceptance audit](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-30-a0052265/dev/log/issues/30/pulls/116/oct24/analysis/requirements.md).

The generated comparison page was verified in Playwright and credits competing plugins and streaming primitives:

![Virtual command lifecycle comparison](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-30-a0052265/docs/screenshots/virtual-command-comparison.png?raw=true)

Final CI on `2288128aa48adeee8235b4923fd940f0b503c2b0` (runs created October 24, 2026 at 22:10:25–22:10:26 UTC): **49 checks passed, six release-only jobs skipped, zero failed or pending**. All eight workflows completed successfully, including [JavaScript/Deno](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40137403818), [Rust on Linux/macOS/Windows and package build](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40137403647), security, parity, benchmarks, workflow hygiene, dependency freshness and repository quality. The [Deno log](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40137403818/job/121002024639) confirms mandatory checkout assertions passed before the verified storage-outage warning. The [Linux regression](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40137403647/job/121002120916) passed with both injected Git starts taking three seconds; the [Windows integration tests](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40137403647/job/121002120988) also passed.

The latest `main` (`5e58fc7012ac35c8e392bd5d4cc04a933a3abaaa`) is included, the working tree is clean, and this PR is ready for review and remains unmerged. CI repair is verified; the external success outcomes listed above remain unfinished.

title: Complete command builder configuration and execution APIs
body:
Literal command descriptions now support fluent, functional, argv-array, constructor and preset styles consistently in JavaScript, with owned fluent/functional builders in Rust. Descriptions remain lazy and reusable, pass arguments directly to the executable, and support synchronous and asynchronous execution.

Fixes #34

```js
await $.command('cat', './some-file.txt')
  .pipe($.command.stdout('inherit'), $.command.exitCode)
  .run();
```

Changes:

- Add immutable argument/configuration methods, nested defaults, configured shell factories and per-execution overrides. Snapshot env/ANSI maps and local-directory arrays; merge explicit environment layers with variable removal. Strict types preserve result selection through long pipelines and reject incompatible transforms.
- Share the builder across full/core ESM and CommonJS entries. Retain the current monorepo and compatibility APIs, with latest main merged.
- Fix native synchronous execution to honor inherited/ignored stdio and disabled capture. Inherited output appears once, inherited stdin reaches the child, and piped output still emits events when capture is disabled. Sync buffering and cancellation limits are documented.
- Extend Rust builders with composition, native environment maps/clear/removal and synchronous execution. Replay environment changes in order using native key comparison, including Windows case-insensitive names. Share native configuration across sync/async and drain output concurrently with buffered stdin.
- Add the [builder guide](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-34-389ba67e/js/docs/COMMAND-BUILDER.md), [library-wide JavaScript comparison](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-34-389ba67e/js/docs/COMPARISON.md) and [per-project Rust comparison](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-34-389ba67e/rust/docs/COMPARISON.md). Cover all twelve JavaScript and fourteen Rust projects in the published audits, plus the issue's Effect reference, across execution, I/O, configuration, lifecycle, shell, streams and development tools. Update stale audit claims and map environment-clear/removal units to executable ports in both exact ledgers.
- Prepare JavaScript and Rust minor releases with the existing release fragments.

Reproduction and regression coverage:

- Original focused tests failed for missing fluent methods, argv/options and preset construction, ignored run options and missing Rust composition/environment methods. Tests now execute the exact issue example, hostile argv and executable paths, reusable descriptions, configuration precedence, stdio, streams, pipelines, deadlines and cancellation. Rust includes a 160 KiB input/output case to detect pipe deadlocks.
- Follow-up tests first failed for sync stdio/capture/inherited stdin, mutable nested presets and unsound long-pipeline types. Runtime and strict type regressions remain in the normal suites. A portable Rust fixture exercises environment clear/remove/re-add and native key semantics in sync/async; Windows CI checks its platform-specific branch.

Validation:

- Full Bun suite: **2,899 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed**; standalone Node builder suite: **7 passed**.
- Rust all-features suite: **962 passed, 7 ignored, 0 failed** in the full serial run.
- Remote validation on `0acfa3d52ae7b8b4b24504f5d11385a264735c89`: **49 checks passed** across all eight workflows; six release-only jobs were skipped as expected. Every run was created at 2026-10-24 12:37:39 UTC, after the commit at 12:37:19 UTC. This includes Node 22/24/26, Bun, Rust on Linux/macOS/Windows, package validation, security, benchmarks and repository checks. The [Windows Rust log](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40094709795/job/120874766276) confirms the native environment-key regression passed. [All CI checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/pull/113/checks).
- JavaScript lint, formatting, duplication and strict TypeScript checks; Rust formatting, all-target/all-feature Clippy and rustdoc with warnings denied.
- All 37 JavaScript/Rust feature examples pass parity checks; generated documentation and relative documentation links are checked.
- The first parallel Rust run hit the existing intermittent cancellation assertion at `cancelled_output.rs:105`. Its focused rerun and full serial suite pass without increasing deadlines; evidence is recorded below.
- Playwright verification from the initial implementation checks all five comparison alternatives and horizontal overflow. The subsequent changes add Markdown documentation and runtime/type regressions.

The comparison credits competitors' strengths and records specialized contracts and runtime limits. It establishes coverage of the published discovery sets; it does not claim unmeasured universal performance superiority or complete upstream API conformance.

The comparison page before and after correcting competitor support:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Previous comparison](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-34-389ba67e/docs/screenshots/command-builder-before.png?raw=true) | ![Corrected comparison](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-34-389ba67e/docs/screenshots/command-builder-after.png?raw=true) |

[Requirement and root-cause evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-34-389ba67e/dev/log/issues/34/pulls/113/analysis/requirements.md).

title: Implement $fy migration for shell and competitor scripts (JS + Rust)
body:
`$fy` now converts shell scripts and competitor JavaScript into executable command-stream modules in both JavaScript and Rust. Shell translation automatically loads command-stream through `use-m`; competitor translation uses the matching command-stream compatibility entry points.

Fixes #1

### Resulting behavior

```sh
npm install use-m
npx command-stream fy deploy.sh deploy.mjs
node deploy.mjs staging
command-stream fy old-zx.mjs migrated.mjs
printf 'import { execa } from "execa";' | command-stream fy --from execa
```

- The default shell rule retains the complete source and selected interpreter, passes arguments/stdin through, and preserves exit status. Generated modules use `await use('command-stream')`; `--no-use-m` supports an already installed library. File translation retains the source basename for `$0`.
- JavaScript ASTs and Rust JavaScript syntax trees identify static imports, re-exports, literal dynamic imports and CommonJS calls for zx, Execa, ShellJS, cross-spawn and Bun's shell API. Rules select corresponding `command-stream/*` entry points while preserving surrounding source. `.cjs`/`--commonjs` produces an executable ES module using `createRequire`, preserving top-level `this` and exports identity.
- Both front ends formalize into actual meta-language `LinkNetwork` syntax/token links, then apply `LinkQuery` and `TranslationRuleSet` substitutions. The structural shell compiler remains available with `--structural`; current main's root `fy()` helper and compatibility APIs remain intact.
- Shared shell, structural, competitor and CommonJS fixtures enforce byte-for-byte JavaScript/Rust output parity. Diagnostics cover unsupported competitor subpaths and locally bound `require`; comments, ordinary strings, regexes and property calls are preserved. Output files cannot overwrite existing files.
- Merged current `main`, including the lightweight core and Rust 1.10.1 release. `$fy` is registered in the shared core without loading the compiler eagerly; cold ESM/CommonJS entry points remain within the 100-module budget. Updated CLI/API documentation and executable examples, and retained minor-release changeset/changelog triggers for both packages.

### Review requirements

The [July review](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/pull/133#issuecomment-5078981845) and [October follow-up](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/pull/133#issuecomment-6380875780) are addressed by the formalize/substitute implementation, competitor migrations, default use-m output and resolved merge. Representation/evaluation separation and composable rules were informed by relative-meta-logic and formal-ai; neither adds a runtime dependency.

Rechecked published meta-language packages: npm `latest` remains 0.46.0; Rust is now 1.0.0. Rust's public dynamic-arity insertion replaces the old chunk-node workaround. Remaining evaluator differences are documented with executable probes in [the integration findings](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-1-7de9505b/js/docs/meta-language-gaps.md) and reported in [the upstream recheck](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/183#issuecomment-6382007356). Translation works independently of further upstream releases. Rust meta-language 1.0.0 still pins tree-sitter to 0.27.0 exactly; the existing freshness exception policy accepts the documented [open upstream blocker](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/197#issuecomment-6382129935).

The latest main release run also exposed changeset merging before remote synchronization. Merging now happens inside the version script after synchronization. A real Git regression with two pending changesets and a concurrent Rust release reproduces the original dirty-tree rebase failure and passes with the corrected order. The downloaded [main failure log](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40081061680) records the exact error at `ci-logs/main-javascript-40081061680.log:51286`.

### Reproduction and validation

`fixtures/fy/competitors.js` previously had no source migration path; `fixtures/fy/sample.sh` did not produce the requested use-m module. Their expected generated modules now have shared JavaScript/Rust regression tests. `fixtures/fy/commonjs.cjs` also reproduces the formerly incorrect top-level `this` binding; its generated module must preserve the original exports identity. Runtime tests execute all five competitor migrations in Node and Bun, compare shell functions/arguments/stdin/status with the original interpreter, and exercise the actual use-m loader and both JS CLI entry points. Native Rust tests cover CLI/stdin, virtual `$fy`, output safety and identical fixtures.

Local validation:

- Full JavaScript suite after the core merge: 2,871 passed, 10 existing skips. The final 216 workflow/release regressions also pass, including a concurrent-release Git reproduction; the 54 focused core/translator tests and five Node core tests pass. Migration runtime tests cover CommonJS binding in Node and Bun.
- Node process/entry-point regression suite after the core merge: 124 passed.
- Full Rust suite including doctests after the Rust 1.10.1 merge: 958 passed, 7 existing ignores; final migration/CLI integration suites passed.
- ESLint, Prettier, duplication checks, TypeScript declarations, frozen Bun install, Rust formatting and Clippy passed.
- Cross-runtime parity: all 37 features pass in JS and Rust, with Node/Bun observations matching; all 39 generated documentation files are current.
- Rust documentation and final verified crate packaging pass (230 files, 494.5 KiB compressed for Rust 1.10.1).

All 49 [PR checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/pull/133/checks) pass on `f5c5ee813f369bdd94ff3fbec2263607171702ac`, including Linux/macOS/Windows test matrices, Node 22/24/26 checks, release build and verified packaging, benchmarks, parity, dependency freshness and security. Failed-run logs were downloaded and checked against commit timestamps and SHAs: the [benchmark locked-build failure](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40078904274) (`ci-logs/benchmarks-40078904274.log:639`) reported `cannot update the lock file ... because --locked was passed` and required refreshing its dependency graph; [generated docs](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40078904294) (`ci-logs/parity-40078904294.log:805`) reported `Generated documentation is out of date` and required the updated virtual-command catalog; [freshness](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079434519) (`ci-logs/dependencies-40079434519.log:756`) reported pending lockfile updates and required updating the benchmark's compatible smallvec version. Execa and fancy-regex were updated to their latest releases, and the resolved Execa type blocker was removed. CodeQL's shebang backtracking finding is fixed with a line parser, a bounded scaling probe and a regression test; GitHub now marks the alert fixed.

See [the translator guide](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-1-7de9505b/js/docs/FY.md) for options, supported entry points and runtime requirements. JavaScript input means standard JavaScript (TypeScript should be compiled first); Bun migration targets its shell API. Keep migrated files beside their inputs when relative imports depend on that location.

title: feat(js): add lightweight core shell entry with an import budget
body:
Adds `command-stream/core` so shell-only consumers can use `$`, ProcessRunner and virtual commands without loading compatibility layers, terminals or development tools. Core loads 70 ESM / 71 CommonJS modules, compared with 284 for the full entry.

Fixes #235

## Changes

- Share the existing shell implementation, built-in commands, registrations, settings and runner identity between the full entry, typed ESM/CommonJS core entries and `process-runner`.
- Separate virtual-command composition and metadata from the package installer that imports Execa.
- Enforce fewer than 100 cold-loaded non-builtin modules in both core formats. Reject compatibility, terminal, REPL/debugger and testing modules in the graph; bundle and execute core without those inputs.
- Document the public core API and prepare its minor release with a changeset.
- Update Execa to 10.2.1 after [its strict TypeScript blocker](https://github.com/sindresorhus/execa/issues/1265) closed. Update fancy-regex and both Rust lockfiles to fix dependency freshness checks, with a Rust patch fragment.
- Retry Deno imports only when esm.sh reports HTTP 408 while a cold build is queued: at most three attempts, with 5- and 10-second delays. Preserve live stderr and a bounded diagnostic tail; persistent timeouts, compiler errors and runtime failures remain fatal. Both real HTTP probes remain required.

The issue explicitly allows the lightweight-subpath approach. The full API remains available; installed dependency size is unchanged. The `parity-exempt` label applies to JavaScript's module-loader graph, which has no Rust counterpart. Executable language parity checks remain enabled.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

Run `node experiments/issue-235/import-probe.mjs command-stream` or substitute `command-stream/core`. Before implementation, the full entry loaded 284 modules in approximately 461 ms on Linux / Node 26.12.1. Commit `7bb8fe2` preserves four failing core regressions before the subpath existed. Module count is the deterministic CI budget; elapsed time is diagnostic.

`core-entry.test.mjs` checks fresh ESM/CommonJS loads, the module budget, executable bundling, real commands, synchronous and exact-argv execution, virtual pipelines, shared state and API identity. Strict TypeScript consumers verify both declaration formats.

The [previous Deno failure](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40077631780/job/120825515833) belongs to `285f44b`, created 2026-10-24T08:20:11Z. Downloaded job-log line 550 reports an esm.sh Execa import returning HTTP 408; line 565 records exit code 1. The same dependency import and immutable GitHub-head URL failed locally, and the CDN status endpoint confirmed queued builds. The queue subsequently recovered and both real probes passed locally. Ten mocked regression tests verify retry success, exhaustion, ANSI diagnostics and immediate failure for other errors. No manual action is required.

## Validation

- Full Bun suite: **2,812 passed, 10 skipped, zero failures** across 179 files, including all ten CDN retry regressions.
- Node core budget, bundling, execution and shared-state checks: **5 passed**.
- Both real Deno CDN probes passed locally, exercising the HTTP-served checkout and immutable GitHub head, shell execution, ShellJS identity, normal brace globs and depth protection.
- Lint, formatting, duplication and strict TypeScript checks passed. The pre-commit hook also passed.
- Existing Node regression suite: **124 passed**; zx: **490 passed, 2 skipped**; Execa: **38 passed**.
- Rust all-feature suite including doctests: **905 passed, 7 ignored**. Formatting, Clippy and rustdoc with warnings denied, and generated documentation checks passed.
- Declared and installed dependency freshness checks passed. Package dry-run includes the core source files and both declaration formats.

CI on `4f88be8eb7d7fa93cd84410cbc1c2933de003f2c`: **49 passed, zero failed or pending**, with six release-only jobs correctly skipped on this PR. All eight workflows completed successfully:

- [JavaScript checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451213), including the [Deno CDN check](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451213/job/120830175205), all Node/Bun platform suites and production-install modes.
- [Rust checks and package validation](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451166), including Linux, macOS and Windows.
- [Dependency freshness](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451195), [repository quality](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451186), [language parity](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451135), [workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451176), [benchmarks](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451143) and [security](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451146).

Downloaded Deno job-log lines 605–608 and 625–628 confirm both real probes executed all assertions successfully. The first Windows Rust attempt stalled in the existing PID-identity test and was cancelled for log collection; the [targeted rerun](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451166/job/120832921106) passed on the same commit, including that test and all doctests. Both attempts' logs are preserved locally. No checks were disabled or relaxed.

The latest default branch is included, the working tree is clean, and the complete diff has been reviewed. Implementation and verification are complete; this PR is ready for review and remains unmerged.

title: Address issues #226–#232: trusted publishing, timeout, non-login shell, env removal, live stdin, artifact selection, detached spawn
body:
## Summary

This PR resolves all seven open issues (#226–#232) as #233 asks. Each requirement is mapped to its implementation and to a test that reproduces the problem without the change in [`dev/log/issues/233/pulls/234/analysis/requirements.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-233-b89721e32913/dev/log/issues/233/pulls/234/analysis/requirements.md).

### #226: crates.io trusted publishing
- The `release` and `instant-release` jobs in `.github/workflows/rust.yml` get `id-token: write`.
- They run `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action` (pinned to v1.0.5) with `continue-on-error: true`.
- They publish with `steps.crates_auth.outputs.token || secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN || secrets.CARGO_TOKEN`. This follows the issue's policy comment: OIDC first, token secrets kept as the fallback.
- `.github/scripts/publish-preflight.mjs` checks the OIDC token first (`js/tests/publish-preflight.test.mjs`).
- The setup is documented in `.github/DEPLOYMENT.md`.

### #227: `$({ timeout })`
- The JS `timeout` option (ms) covers simple commands, pipelines, `stream()`, exec specs and `.sync()`.
- It combines with a caller `signal`, reports `result.timedOut`, and rejects invalid values with a `TypeError`.
- Rust parity: `RunOptions::timeout`, `StreamingRunner::timeout` and `timed_out()`.
- Tests: `js/tests/timeout-option.test.mjs`, `rust/tests/timeout.rs`.

### #228: non-login shell by default
- Command strings now run with `sh -c` instead of `-l -c`, so profile files no longer print into captured output or override the `PATH` from `env`.
- `loginShell: true` restores the old behaviour.
- `js/tests/login-shell.test.mjs` uses the issue's `HOME`/`.profile` reproduction.

### #229: removing environment variables
- Rust:
  - `RunOptions::env_remove`
  - `StreamingRunner::env_remove`/`env_remove_all`
  - `TerminalCaptureOptions::env_remove`/`env_clear`, forwarded to `portable_pty::CommandBuilder`
- JS: an `env` value of `undefined` removes that variable from the child.
- Tests: `rust/tests/env_remove.rs`, `rust/tests/terminal_options.rs` (the issue's `SECRET_TOKEN` case), `js/tests/env-undefined-removes.test.mjs`.

### #230: live stdin with an exact argv (Rust)
- `StreamingRunner::stdin_pipe()` keeps stdin open. `OutputStream::write_stdin`/`close_stdin` work while output streams.
- `ProcessRunner::from_argv(program, args, options)` skips the shell and virtual commands.
- Tests: `rust/tests/stdin_pipe.rs`, `rust/tests/process_argv.rs`.

### #231: terminal artifact selection
- JS `artifacts: [...]` and Rust `TerminalCaptureOptions::artifacts` select the files to write. Renderers for unselected files are skipped, so no GIF is rendered unless one is asked for.
- Rust also gets:
  - `recording.gif`, encoded with `gif` and drawn with `font8x8` glyphs, so no SVG rasteriser is needed;
  - `aspect_ratio`;
  - `on_trace`.
- Tests: `js/tests/terminal-artifact-selection.test.mjs`, `rust/tests/terminal_options.rs`.

### #232: fire-and-forget detached spawn
- JS `spawnDetached()`, `runner.spawnDetached()` and `$({ detached: true })`:
  - start the command in its own session with ignored stdio and `unref()`;
  - resolve with `{ pid }` on `spawn` and reject on `error`.
- Rust `StreamingRunner::detach()` and `ProcessRunner::spawn_detached()` do the same.
- Tests: `js/tests/detached-spawn.test.mjs` (pid = pgid, session leader, outlives the caller), `rust/tests/detach.rs`.

Docs, feature-catalog examples (JS Node/Bun and Rust, checked by `scripts/check-parity.mjs`), a changeset and a Rust changelog fragment are included.

## CI fixes needed along the way

| Check | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JS tests on Bun 1.4.4 | Bun 1.4.4 replaced the glob matcher that `js/src/bun-shell/glob.mjs` ports, and nesting is no longer limited to 10 levels | The test checks the ported v1.4.2 limit directly (probe: `experiments/issue-233/bun-glob-nesting.mjs`) |
| JS tests on macOS | macOS `ps` has no `sid` keyword | The session leader is read from the `s` in `ps -o stat` |
| Benchmarks `--locked` | `gif`/`font8x8` were missing from `rust/benchmarks/Cargo.lock` | Lockfile updated |
| Language parity | Bumping tokio in `rust/benchmarks/Cargo.toml` counted as a Rust benchmark change, but JS benchmark dependencies live in `js/package.json`, which is never counted | `.github/scripts/check-language-parity.sh` treats the benchmark manifest like its lockfile. A new benchmark target still adds a source file and is caught (`js/tests/language-parity.test.mjs`) |
| Dependency freshness (also red on `main`) | Newer releases of eslint, eslint-plugin-prettier, jscpd, tokio, libc, vt100, ureq and execa | All updated except execa. vt100 0.18 takes `NonZeroU16` sizes and returns `String` state, and terminal capture converts at that boundary. vt100 is not part of the public API |

### execa is held at 10.1.1
execa 10.2.0's own declarations fail to type-check with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and `skipLibCheck: false`:

```
TS2344 in types/return/result-all.d.ts: Types of property 'preferLocal' are incompatible.
```

command-stream re-exports those types and checks them with these settings.

- I reported it upstream: https://github.com/sindresorhus/execa/issues/1265. The minimal reproduction is in `experiments/issue-233/execa-types/`.
- Because JSON has no comments, the freshness check now reads npm blockers from `js/dependency-blockers.json`. The blocker counts only while its issue is open.
- The bare `npm outdated` step became `bun scripts/check-dependencies.mjs --installed-npm`. That step still fails when a lockfile falls behind its declaration (tests in `js/tests/dependency-freshness.test.mjs`).

## Maintainer step after merge (#226)
Register the trusted publisher on crates.io:

```
package-registry-manager setup --registry crates-io --migrate --execute
```

Until then, releases keep publishing through the token fallback.

## Verification
